persons.name: Col. Jean Baptiste Beaubien

occupation.note: 'J. B. Beaubien, merchant' in the 1833 roster; a licensed trader from the county court's earliest permits - the clerk 'granted permits to sell goods to Alexander Robinson, John B. Beaubien, and Madore B. Beaubien' in 1831 - and before that the American Fur Company's man at Chicago.

persons.note: HE CAME TO CHICAGO AND BOUGHT THE CABIN AND CULTIVATED FIELD SOUTH OF THE OLD FORT IN 1812, and the house remained his residence until 1839. He was a trader at Milwaukee as early as 1800. He was one of the twenty-eight electors of 10 August 1833 and took six votes for trustee. HIS TWO MARRIAGES ARE DOCUMENTED AND THEY ARE WHY THIS HOUSEHOLD IS FLAGGED: he married first Mah-naw-bun-no-quah, an Ottawa woman, the mother of his sons Charles Henry and Madore; and in 1812 he married Josette LaFramboise, daughter of Francois LaFramboise, of an influential French trading family. THE TOWN'S OWN ROLLS, 1833-1835 — CORROBORATION, NOT A GRADE. The early Chicago voter and tax lists held by the Illinois Regional Archives Depository name this person 2 times: Poll list of the first election of the Board of Trustees of the Town of Chicago, 10 August 1833 — “Beaubien, J. B.” (poll_1833_003, line 24); Poll list of 1835 — “Beaubien, Col. J. B.” (poll_1835_005, line 290). These are the town's own contemporary paper rather than a recollection of it, and each appearance says that a man of that name stood on that roll in that year — no more. The reading is twice mediated (Schulz's transcription, then Genealogy Trails' republication) and this project has not seen the IRAD originals. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) the 1835 poll with a second independent source is attested, the 1835 poll alone or a 1833/1834 list with another source is inferred, and a single appearance with nothing else is a projected resident. This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE — T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: one resident of the surname 'Beaubien' agrees with the entry's forenames; 4 bearer(s) of the surname were considered. (data/research/civic/voter_crosswalk.json).

persons.note: NAMED AND DATED IN THE SOURCE - married to J. B. Beaubien in 1812, daughter of Francois LaFramboise - and nothing places her in the household on 1 July 1835. She is written because a named wife of a named head is exactly the person this layer exists to record, and graded derived because the presence on the day is the reconstruction. The LaFramboise family is separately in the 1833 treaty schedules, where 'Joseph Laframboise and children' receive $1,000.

persons.note: AN ADMISSION. J. B. Beaubien's family was large and is not enumerated in anything reached; two sons are named in Andreas and one of them, Madore, has his own household here. Carried as one placeholder rather than as invented individuals; do not count it as a person.

research_note: THE OLDEST HOUSEHOLD IN THE 1835 TOWN AND THE ONE THAT MOST NEEDS THE REMOVAL FLAG. J. B. Beaubien's first wife was an Ottawa woman and his sons by her are among the town's merchants; his second wife's family is in the 1833 treaty's schedule of payments; his homestead stands on a military reservation he was claiming from the United States in the scene year. Every one of those facts touches the dispossession that was completed in August 1835, six weeks after the scene date. THE RECORD MAKES NO CLAIM ABOUT ANY PERSON'S IDENTITY, AFFILIATION OR STATUS beyond what Andreas states, and it is flagged for review under the project's standing constraint rather than treated as settled. Note also what this household is NOT: a Potawatomi household. It is a French-descended trading family with Native kin, which is a distinct and much better-documented category, and collapsing the two would be the first step towards exactly the improvisation AGENTS.md forbids.

directories.note: LATER EVIDENCE, BESIDE THE 1835 CLAIMS AND NOT INSIDE THEM. A Chicago directory of 1839, 1843 or 1844 meets somebody of this name and this pass records what it prints. Under the ratified ladder a directory read after 1835 can corroborate that a person attested here was still in Chicago and can print a trade or a street the 1835 record never had; on its own it makes nobody a resident of 1835. Nothing on this person's 1835 record was regraded, moved, dated or given an occupation by this entry.
